Cc: Marcus Li <m.li@aurigahealth.com>

Subject: Production spike after model v4.2Q rollout

Hi Aditya —

We started seeing a customer-impacting spike right after the v4.2Q rollout at ~08:50 PST. Quick summary: p99 latency from ~180ms -> ~420ms, 95th ~210ms -> ~380ms, error rate (5xx/timeout) jumped to 3.2% (baseline ~0.2%), and effective throughput is down ~28% on our hot endpoints. This is across our authentication and payments paths — we are seeing request retries from clients that are compounding the load.

Attached is a small upload of logs and a timeline (prod-sla-logs-1107.tar.gz). We pushed the v4.2Q quant profile per the runbook at 08:30. Can you triage ASAP and set up a bridge? This is hitting revenue flows.

— Sofia
Senior Product Ops, Auriga Health

On Sat, Nov 7, 2026 at 9:20 AM Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks Sofia — sorry for the disruption. I’ve spun up a bridge for 09:00 PST...

Quick engineering readout from initial traces:
- The v4.2Q rollout switched Auriga’s endpoints to the new "q-fast" quant profile that uses aggressive fused attention kernels. On our A100 fleet we are seeing a fallback path where the fused kernels are not used for sequences >512, which forces a slower attention kernel and extra memory copies. That matches the p99 jump.
- Error spikes appear as timeouts from the serving runtime while waiting on KV-cache warmups; concurrent retries are creating a thundering effect on downstream model workers.
- Preliminary mitigation options (fast -> safe):
  1) Pin traffic back to v4.1 (current live binary) for the critical routes (auth, payments) — high confidence, immediate effect.
  2) Switch Auriga to the "q-stable" quant profile for v4.2Q (fallback to safer kernel paths) — medium confidence, quick to flip.
  3) Reduce max-batch-size to 4 and temporarily disable prefix prefetch (prefetch_kv=false) — short-term risk to throughput but could reduce latency.

I’m attaching the kernel trace and a short log excerpt (kernel-trace-1107.txt). If the team approves, we should do option 1 (pin to v4.1) for >60% of critical traffic and monitor for 30m; then iterate to a better q-profile.

— Irene
SRE, Redwood Inference
